draft.title: Alternative methods of sentencing
card: Alternative methods of sentencing involve more people than the judge and the lawyers. They aim to deal with the harm caused by an offence and the reasons behind it.
Aboriginal elders and community members sit with the magistrate, the offender and often the victim. They talk together and help decide the sentence for an Aboriginal offender.
The offender and the victim are brought together, often in a conference. The offender hears how the offence affected the victim and can take responsibility and try to repair the harm.
Both methods give the community or the victim a voice in the process. A traditional court hearing is mainly between the court, the prosecution and the accused.
draft.remember: Circle sentencing involves elders and community. Restorative justice involves the victim and offender meeting.

a.q: Which feature is found in circle sentencing but not in a traditional court hearing?
opts: Aboriginal elders help decide the sentence
The magistrate alone decides the sentence
The prosecution presents the case against the accused
The offender is brought before a court
a.why: In circle sentencing, Aboriginal elders and community members take part in sentencing an Aboriginal offender. A magistrate, a prosecution and an offender in court are also found in traditional hearings, so they do not set circle sentencing apart.
a.clue: Think about who sits in the circle besides the magistrate.

b.q: Dan damaged a neighbour's fence. A conference is arranged where he hears how it affected the neighbour and offers to repair it. What is this method?
opts: Restorative justice
Circle sentencing
Parole
An appeal
b.why: Restorative justice brings the offender and the victim together so the offender can face the harm and try to repair it. Circle sentencing is the tempting wrong answer: it involves elders and community members sentencing an Aboriginal offender, and nothing here says that.
b.clue: Look at who Dan meets in the conference.

a.best: Aboriginal elders help decide the sentence

problems.detail: The remember line ties the victim only to restorative justice. The card says the victim often takes part in circle sentencing too, so the remember line splits the two methods more neatly than the card does.

check.summary: The facts and both questions are sound. The one minor issue is that the remember line leaves out that victims often take part in circle sentencing, which separates the two methods more neatly than the card does.
